trust_decision.summary: Whether a sourceMappingURL annotation taken from CSS text may name a file that PostCSS reads is decided once, in PreviousMap.loadFile, on the path after loadMap joins it to dirname(opts.from); a program-supplied map.prev callback bypasses that check, and a process option (unsafeMap) turns it off.

landing_point.why: The advisory is about an attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL in CSS comments; this branch is the only place where that annotation is turned into a filesystem path and handed to loadFile, which then calls existsSync/readFileSync.

fix_sites.module_kind: core library class (trusted program-supplied callback route)

fix_sites.entry_point: postcss.parse(css, {from}) with an annotation in the CSS (lib/previous-map.js:124-128)
fix_sites.module_kind: core library class (untrusted annotation route, plus JSONP prefix strip)

fix_sites.entry_point: root.source.input.map.consumer() and Input#origin (lib/input.js:74, lib/input.js:207); PreviousMap is a public subpath export (package.json:66)
Processor#process(css, {unsafeMap: true}) - new opt-out read in the PreviousMap constructor (lib/previous-map.js:17-19)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report only shows a sourceMappingURL comment arriving through postcss.parse / Processor#process, so PreviousMap - a separately exported class (package.json:66, lib/previous-map.d.ts:12-19) that library authors construct directly (test/map.test.ts:24) - reads as a lower-level API outside the advisory's scope, and its own annotation handling is left unguarded.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The documented map.prev callback (typed as (file: string) => string) and map.prev given as a string of map content must keep loading maps whose path does not end in .map, and inline data:application/json URIs must keep working; a blanket extension check inside loadFile breaks the callback route, which is why the published fix threads a trusted flag and an unsafeMap opt-out instead.

O6_input_shapes: relative annotation path with a non-.map extension (e.g. a.css) - must not be read
absolute annotation path with a non-.map extension (e.g. /etc/passwd) - must not be read
annotation ending in .map or .MAP (case-insensitive) - still read
annotation that is an inline data:application/json URI - unchanged, still decoded
map.prev as a function returning any path, .map or not - still read (trusted)
map.prev as string / plain object / SourceMapConsumer / SourceMapGenerator - unchanged
unsafeMap: true process option - replaces the extension check
.map file whose text begins with a )]}' JSONP/XSSI line - prefix stripped before JSON.parse
.map file whose text is not valid JSON - previous map silently dropped instead of throwing

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second Input/PreviousMap built from the original CSS inside the source-map generator (line 296)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Map generation already re-creates an Input here to collect previous maps, so a maintainer adding a map-reload or 'refresh annotation' step while regenerating maps would naturally put it in this module instead of the parser.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: re-hydrating a PreviousMap from serialized state and re-reading its mapFile/annotation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: fromJSON already rebuilds PreviousMap instances with PreviousMap.prototype; a maintainer adding validation or a disk reload for restored maps would add it at this boundary.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: resolving map source/sourceRoot entries into filesystem paths (mapResolve)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is where map data is already turned into paths, so refusing sources that escape the map root would realistically be written next to it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an Input built from raw CSS with no process options while rendering an error
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already constructs an Input without opts (so opts.map/unsafeMap cannot reach it), and it is a separate, easily overlooked consumer of PreviousMap.

O9_family: arbitrary local file read / path traversal leading to information disclosure (CWE-22, CWE-200)

O10_build.language: JavaScript (CommonJS lib/, ESM wrapper lib/postcss.mjs, TypeScript type tests)
O10_build.toolchain: Node.js ^10 || ^12 || >=14 (package.json:145-147); pnpm, uvu test runner with ts-node/register, tsc/check-dts for types, eslint; no native deps (nanoid, picocolors, source-map-js)
O10_build.project_tests: uvu suites cover this area: test/previous-map.test.ts (annotation reads at :170-194, prev callback at :224-267, inline data URIs at :86-143), test/map.test.ts, test/input.test.ts, test/fromJSON.test.ts; run with `pnpm unit` (or `pnpm test`).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `if (!/\.map$/i.test(path)) return undefined` at the top of loadFile, or strip the annotation before PreviousMap is built, which silently kills the documented map.prev callback route (lib/postcss.d.ts:306) and drops non-.map previous maps for legitimate build tools.

unverified: Repo size in MB could not be measured (no shell in this session); lib/ is ~40 small files and the whole tree without node_modules looks well under 5 MB, so tiny_repo is asserted from inspection, not measurement.
Whether the GHSA/CVE and its fix are widely written up (O13) could not be checked offline; medium is a judgement from postcss's popularity.
The published loadFile signature gains a cssFile parameter (fix.diff:82) that is never referenced in the new body (fix.diff:83-92); its intended use is unclear.
No test files are added or changed by either fix commit, so the hidden behavioural scope (e.g. whether unsafeMap is expected to be tested) is inferred from the diff only.

The terminal-highlight path (lib/terminal-highlight.js:51 -> new Input(css) -> PreviousMap) reaches the same sink but is only realistically attacker-reachable via CssSyntaxError#showSourceCode on an erroring line, so it was not counted in O1.
